clue.text: Acquire Dutch courage from blended snifter when loud earl gatecrashes …

indicators.note: a gatecrasher pushes into a party uninvited, so these letters push into the middle of the others
a blended drink has its ingredients mixed together, so the letters of snifter are mixed into a new order

parts.note: F (forte) is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink for courage before a rowdy aristocrat barges into the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gatecrashes' puts F and E inside a rearrangement of SNIFTER, the anagram signalled by 'blended'. The clue runs on with an ellipsis into 8 Across, which has nothing to do with this wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch courage is confidence got from alcohol, and a stiff drink taken to brace yourself is called this.

clue.text: Teeth reset oddly — that's a 'laugh'!

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: Someone has had their teeth reset, and finds it funny.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee-hee is a giggle or titter, a kind of snigger.

clue.text: Far off and very quietly, Earth becomes iced

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters of far are reordered

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quietly

explanation.surface: Far away and in silence, the planet freezes over.
explanation.definitionFit: Frappé describes a drink served chilled or with crushed ice.

clue.text: First alternative steel band exclude absent …

indicators.note: an alternative version is a different arrangement, so the letters are reordered
absent means the synonym is missing from the word band

parts.note: to ban someone is to exclude them

explanation.surface: A first-choice alternative steel band is shut out of the line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absent' strikes BAN from BAND to leave D; 'alternative' rearranges STEEL plus D.
explanation.definitionFit: The firstborn child of a family is the eldest, the oldest one.

clue.text: … male lead from 'Islands', tipped off in message

indicators.note: tipped off as in knocked over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order
the lead from a word is its first letter, here of Islands

explanation.surface: Continuing from 4 Down, the male lead of a show called Islands is tipped off in a message.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail is a message sent between computers.

clue.text: Trade organisation from '51 — extremely comprehensive one

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
extremely means very
comp is short for a comprehensive school
any means one, as in 'any one will do'

explanation.surface: A trade body dating from 1951, very comprehensive in scope.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British state secondary school open to all abilities, often shortened to comp.
explanation.definitionFit: The City of London guilds of trades and crafts are known as this, after their ceremonial dress.

clue.text: Pet film star on set, being bumptious

indicators.note: set means arranged or put in place, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A pampered movie star on set is behaving pompously.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumptious and self-important both describe someone conceited and pushy.

clue.text: … top-level gathering — maybe grouse season's beginning?

parts.note: high ground, top-level terrain, is highland
grouse is an example of game, birds shot for sport

indicators.note: the beginning of the word season gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Following the ellipsis, a lofty social gathering seems to be the opening of the grouse-shooting season.
explanation.walkthrough: Highland Games are Scottish open-air sports meetings with caber tossing, hammer throwing and piping; 'Highland gathering' is their traditional name. The grouse season opens on 12 August, the 'Glorious Twelfth'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland gathering is the traditional Scottish term for this event of sport, music and dance.

clue.text: Distant photos viewed in 3 spells?

parts.note: a distant manner is cold and aloof
snaps are casual photographs

explanation.surface: Faraway pictures seem to be magic spells viewed through ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 Down is FRAPPE, iced, so the definition is iced spells: periods of freezing weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold snap is a sudden short spell of freezing weather.

clue.text: Overheard: Take cover, Jack — it's getting wet

indicators.note: overheard means the words are heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: to take cover is to hide, and a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, a rating

explanation.surface: A sailor is told to shelter because it is raining.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a navy sailor without a commission; jack is slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking on water, or being moistened, is what the word describes.

clue.text: Very big margins in ovenware include incomplete premium

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so the outer pair holds the rest
the margins of a word are its outer letters, here those of ovenware
incomplete means the last letter is lost from the synonym

parts.note: premium quality is the best

explanation.surface: Kitchen-shop talk: the edges of some ovenware dish are paired with a top-quality range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very big' seems to describe the ovenware, but it is the definition; 'premium' means best quality, not a price.
explanation.definitionFit: Obesity is the condition of being grossly overweight, so very big in body.

clue.text: Socialist abandoned chicanery ultimately

parts.note: something abandoned has been left behind

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of chicanery

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician quits in the end over dirty tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial term for someone on the political left, such as a socialist.

clue.text: Orders clubs to wear suits

indicators.note: to wear clothes is to have them around you, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a suit of clothes or of cards is a set, so suits are sets
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Someone is told to dress for the club in proper suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orders' reads as a verb, but it is a plural noun: religious orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious orders and sects are both bodies of believers bound by a shared rule or creed.

clue.text: Singular accent that one will 26 Down at 8

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
an accent or inflection of the voice is a tone

explanation.surface: A one-off accent from someone who will dance a fling at the Highland Games.
explanation.walkthrough: With 26 Down FLING and 8 HIGHLAND GAMES, the definition is something flung at the Games: the stone put.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting the stone, hurling a heavy rock, is a standard heavy event of the Highland Games.

clue.text: Carriage with Queen that's elevated at 8

parts.note: a cab is a carriage for hire
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A royal carriage is lifted aloft at the Highland Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is HIGHLAND GAMES; the caber is a long tree trunk raised upright and tossed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tossing the caber involves hoisting a huge wooden pole and throwing it end over end.

clue.text: Barber's second try?

definitions.note: read as barber's job, a verb: what a barber does to hair

parts.note: a judge will try or hear a case in court

explanation.surface: A barber is asked to have another go at a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting off hair or wool with blades is the work of a barber or sheep clipper.

clue.text: Medic to solver: 'Time to go on the wagon'

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
the solver is addressed as you

explanation.surface: A doctor tells a patient doing the crossword that it is time to stop drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on the wagon means giving up alcohol, as does drying out in rehab.

clue.text: Non-professional pool's unfinished — it's to be launched in 8

parts.note: a ham is an amateur, especially an unskilled actor or radio operator

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: a mere is a pool or small lake

explanation.surface: An amateur's swimming pool isn't completed, though something is to be launched there.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is Highland Games, where throwing the hammer is a standard event.
explanation.definitionFit: At Highland Games the heavy-weight event of throwing this, a ball on a handle, is a classic contest.

clue.text: Show some aplomb, resigning in game

indicators.note: to show some of the words is to display part of their run of letters

explanation.surface: A player concedes the match with good grace and some composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is an old three-handed card game popular in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Traditionalist's recommendations dashed midstream — surprisingly rejected

indicators.note: dashed hopes are wrecked, so the letters of recommendations are broken up and reordered
the letters of midstream are thrown out of that pool in no particular order, which is the surprise

explanation.surface: A conservative's advice gets abandoned halfway through, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike the letters of MIDSTREAM from RECOMMENDATIONS and rearrange the six left over (C, O, E, N, O, N).
explanation.definitionFit: A neoconservative holds right-wing, traditional views, so loosely a traditionalist in politics.

clue.text: Solvent made from active fluid plus grain

parts.note: A is the grammatical abbreviation for active
FL is the abbreviation for fluid, as in fl oz
oat is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A chemistry recipe: a solvent made of a liquid with a grain added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solvent' looks chemical, but here it means financially sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that stays out of debt and can pay its way is said to be keeping its head above water.

clue.text: Slip away with leader in panic

indicators.note: doing away with the leader removes the first letter of the synonym

parts.note: terror is extreme fear or panic

explanation.surface: Someone slips off, taking the ringleader along, amid panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, a synonym for a mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Flush wine cave

parts.note: red is red wine
a den is an animal's cave or lair

explanation.surface: Wine in a cellar is flushed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To flush is to go pink in the face, to blush or colour up.

clue.text: Revealed years in temporary suspension

parts.note: a secret revealed is out
age is a span of years

explanation.surface: A long-hidden fact is revealed after years in a temporary state.
explanation.definitionFit: A period when a power supply or service stops working for a while.

clue.text: Prince surrounded by birds — they sound shrill at 8

indicators.note: to be surrounded by something is to sit inside it

parts.note: pie is an old name for the magpie

explanation.surface: A royal among squawking birds at the Highland Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is Highland Games, where bagpipe playing is a central event.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagpipes make a famously piercing skirl, and piping competitions are part of every such Scottish gathering.

clue.text: Instrument artist tuned endlessly

indicators.note: an instrument tuned has its strings adjusted, so these letters are adjusted into a new order
endlessly means the last letter of artist is lost

explanation.surface: A musician keeps tuning an instrument forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ARTIST to ARTIS, which 'tuned' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian lute played by plucking its strings.

clue.text: Turn over in delightful bed

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: something delightful is fun
TO is the abbreviation for turn over, as in PTO, please turn over

explanation.surface: Rolling over in a lovely bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style padded mattress used as a bed, often on a folding frame.

clue.text: Doubling up, former partner leaves knees-up at 8

indicators.note: when someone leaves, they are gone from the word, so the letters are removed

parts.note: doubling up the arms or legs is bending them, flexing
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Doubled up in laughter as an ex walks out of the party at the Highland Games.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is British slang for a lively party or dance; 8 is HIGHLAND GAMES, where the Highland fling is danced.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highland fling is a lively solo Scottish dance performed in competitions.

clue.text: Noted Tunisian upset peace group

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-known person from Tunisia is upset with a peace organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The world body founded in 1945 to keep international peace and security.

clue.text: Eleanor's maturity, you might say, shows remarkable culture

indicators.note: you might say signals that the words are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: Eleanor Bron is an English actress; her maturity is her age, so Bron's age

explanation.surface: Praise for an older actress whose cultivated manner shows she is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleanor Bron is a British actress known from Help! and Absolutely Fabulous.
explanation.definitionFit: The era of prehistory when bronze tools were made, noted for its striking cultures and metalwork.
